 About Stripe 
 Stripe is a technology company focused on improving the conditions for economic growth and prosperity. We build programmable financial infrastructure, rethinking from first principles how financial services should work, to make it easier and cheaper for any business to start and scale. More than 10 million businesses build on Stripe, spanning the economic frontier—from solo founders to established enterprises—united by a practical focus on growth. When any business can easily serve a global customer base, the quality and diversity of products in the world increase, and craft and creativity are unleashed into the smallest niches. Our own growth is wholly contingent on the success of the businesses building on Stripe. We therefore invest back into our technology at an unusual rate. We make upgrades to our products every single day to deliver compounding gains to our customers. We maintain some of the most reliable APIs on the internet. We build entirely new pieces of financial infrastructure to enable new ideas. And our significant advances in risk and fraud infrastructure over many years are making the internet economy safer and more accessible. 
 Though people at Stripe don’t tend to take themselves seriously, Stripe is a fairly serious place: our customers are depending on us for their livelihoods. About RYSE
 RYSE is an innovative hardware Original Equipment Manufacturer (OEM) based in Toronto, specializing in connected IoT devices and smart automated solutions. We bridge the gap between custom electronics, embedded firmware, and consumer-facing software ecosystems. To help build the brains behind our next generation of smart hardware, we are seeking a passionate and problem-solving Firmware Engineer to join our team.
 The Role
 Working under the guidance and mentorship of senior engineers and the FW/Engineering Manager, you will be responsible for developing, debugging, and maintaining the embedded C code that powers our connected devices.
 While your primary focus will be on feature development and board bring-up, you will also play a critical role in product quality. You will write unit tests, develop Hardware-in-the-Loop (HIL) test routines, and collaborate closely with our QA/Test Engineers to ensure your code is highly testable on the production line. You will leverage modern AI-assisted coding tools to accelerate your development and documentation workflows.
 Key Responsibilities
 Firmware Development: Write, modify, and optimize robust embedded C code for resource-constrained microcontrollers (MCUs) wiht BLE and WiFi applications.
 Firmware Testing & Validation: Develop and execute unit tests, integration tests, and hardware-in-the-loop (HIL) test cases. Ensure all new firmware features are thoroughly validated before being handed off to the QA team.
 Hardware/Software Integration: Participate in initial board bring-up for new R&D prototypes. Intersect software and hardware by reading component datasheets and configuring peripherals (I2C, SPI, UART, ADC/DAC).
 Cross-Functional Testing Support: Work hand-in-hand with the Test Engineering Team to ensure Design for Testability (DFT). Provide them with firmware diagnostic commands and assist in troubleshooting issues found on production test fixtures.
 AI-Enhanced Workflows: Utilize AI-assisted developer tools (e.g., GitHub Copilot, ChatGPT, Claude) to draft boilerplate code, generate unit test frameworks, optimize functions, and write clean technical documentation.
 Bug Tracking & Root-Cause Analysis: Investigate field-reported issues and QA bug tickets. Use lab equipment (oscilloscopes, logic analyzers, debuggers) to trace complex timing, memory, or hardware state issues and deploy fixes.
 Qualifications & Skills
 Experience: 1–2 years of experience in embedded software development or firmware engineering (including relevant internships, co-op terms, practical lab coursework, or personal hardware projects).
 Education: Degree or Diploma in Computer Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Mechatronics, Computer Science, or a related field.
 Programming Languages: Strong proficiency in embedded C for embedded systems. Working knowledge of Python for test scripting and automation.
 Embedded Systems Knowledge: Familiarity with microcontrollers (e.g., ARM Cortex-M, ESP32, Nordic), RTOS concepts, and basic wireless communication protocols (Wi-Fi, Bluetooth/BLE).
 Testing Mindset: Experience or strong interest in C unit testing and a solid understanding of how to test code on physical hardware.
 Lab Equipment: Hands-on familiarity with electronics bench tools (JTAG/SWD debuggers, oscilloscopes, digital multimeters, logic analyzers).
 AI-Assisted Tools: Experience using AI tools for coding, debugging, or test generation.
 Eligibility: Eligible to work in Canada.
 What We Offer
 Comprehensive Benefits: Full Health and Dental coverage.
 Time Off: Generous Paid Time Off (PTO) and company-observed holidays.
 Lab Access: Access to a fully equipped R&D lab and hands-on hardware prototyping environment.
 Mentorship & Growth: Direct, hands-on guidance from senior firmware and systems engineers to accelerate your embedded development career.

ABOUT BASETEN

Baseten powers mission-critical inference for the world's most dynamic AI companies, like Cursor, Notion, OpenEvidence, Abridge, Clay, Gamma, and Writer. By uniting applied AI research, flexible infrastructure, and seamless developer tooling, we enable companies operating at the frontier of AI to bring cutting-edge models into production. We're growing quickly and recently raised our $1.5B Series F https://www.baseten.co/blog/announcing-our-series-f/, led by Altimeter Capital, Conviction Partners, and Spark Capital. Join us and help build the platform engineers turn to ship AI products.

THE ROLE

The AI ecosystem is being built by many companies at once: model labs creating increasingly capable models, hyperscalers providing infrastructure and distribution, developers building new AI products, and a growing ecosystem of tools that agents can use.

Baseten sits at the center of that ecosystem as the inference platform developers use to run AI in production. Partner Engineering is how we connect those worlds.

As one of the first engineers focused on Partner Engineering at Baseten, you'll build the technical foundation behind some of our most strategic relationships. You'll work directly with engineers at leading model labs, hyperscalers, developer platforms, and AI infrastructure companies to turn partnerships into products developers can actually use.

You don't need a previous partner engineering title. We want an engineer who enjoys working directly with another company's technical team and carrying the resulting product decisions into production at Baseten.

WHAT YOU'LL BUILD

 - Bring new capabilities into Baseten. Integrate a search or developer-tools provider into Baseten so an agent can call the service during inference, with consistent authentication, execution, failure handling, observability, and usage reporting.

 - Take Baseten into new distribution channels. Integrate Baseten with a hyperscaler, cloud marketplace, or developer platform so customers can discover models, provision access, and run inference through a partner's product while Baseten handles the underlying serving infrastructure.

 - Launch models with leading model labs. Build the infrastructure that lets developers discover and run a model lab's newest models on Baseten, including access controls, usage attribution, metering, and the systems required to support commercial agreements such as revenue sharing.

 - Create the partner platform itself. Identify the primitives common across these integrations and turn them into reusable platform capabilities so we can launch increasingly sophisticated partnerships without reinventing the stack every time.
   
   

WHAT YOU'LL OWN

 - Lead strategic partner integrations from technical discovery and architecture through implementation, launch, and production operation.

 - Work directly with partner engineering teams to design APIs, define system boundaries, resolve cross-company dependencies, and make architectural decisions.

 - Write substantial production code and own the systems you build.

 - Build reusable partner-platform primitives across identity, provisioning, inference, model serving, metering, billing, and other Baseten platform capabilities.

 - Own technical delivery across Baseten and partner teams, including milestones, dependencies, risks, and architectural tradeoffs.

 - Work closely with Partnerships and Product to understand where the ecosystem is going and translate emerging opportunities into platform investments.

 - Raise the bar for integration reliability through strong API contracts, testing, observability, safe rollouts, and thoughtful failure handling.

 - Help define what Partner Engineering becomes at Baseten as both the team and our ecosystem grow.
   
   

REQUIREMENTS

 - Experience designing, shipping, and operating large-scale distributed systems in production. You can explain the architectural choices you made and how they meet customers' needs at scale.

 - A record of leading ambiguous engineering projects across teams while contributing substantial production code yourself.

 - Sound judgment about API design, service boundaries, and failure handling. You've built systems that uphold API contracts and meet measurable service-level objectives that customers and partners depend on.

 - Experience turning requests from customers, partners, or other engineering teams into a defined technical scope. You can explain a constraint, propose an alternative, and document the decision.

 - Comfort working across application code and cloud infrastructure, including debugging behavior that crosses service boundaries.

NICE TO HAVE

 - Product integrations with cloud providers, developer platforms, or other infrastructure companies.

 - Usage metering, marketplace infrastructure, or commerce systems that support relationships among multiple parties.

 - Model serving or other artificial intelligence (AI) infrastructure used in production.

BENEFITS

 - Competitive compensation, including meaningful equity

 - Paid parental leave

 - Fertility and family-building stipend through Carrot

 - (U.S. only) Company-facilitated 401(k)

Roughly 80% of our revenue comes through that funnel.
 The paid marketing team is led by the Head of Growth and includes our direct response marketers, media buyer and video editors. They set the strategy, write the ads, manage the spend and produce the creative. We need one person to run everything underneath them, and that is this role.
 You will own the weekly numbers the team works from, the project system the work moves through, the checklist every ad passes before it goes live, the landing page and email builds, and the group of video editors who turn scripts into finished ads. Done well, the Head of Growth never has to assemble a report, fix a ClickUp board or ask whether something has shipped.
 This is a new seat. The team will grow, and the systems you build are the ones new joiners will work from. Nobody has held this role full-time before, so part of the job is working out how it should run.
 Why we are hiring 
 At the moment, the reporting, quality checks, page builds and editor coordination are spread across several people who each have other priorities. Nobody has this as their whole job, so the weekly numbers arrive late, compliance gets checked at the final review rather than before it, and builds wait behind copy. We want one full-time person to take all of that and run it properly.

 Reporting. The weekly marketing dashboard and Monday report: spend, cost per call, opt-in rate, return on ad spend, win rate per writer, and the number of ads launched, reconciled across the ad platforms, Hyros, and the CRM.  Systems. Our ClickUp workspace for marketing: the production pipeline, statuses, dashboards, templates, and the intake from Slack. Written procedures and naming conventions for every repeatable process. An asset library organised well enough that nobody has to search Google Drive.
 Quality control. A compliance and QA checklist on every ad and email before it reaches the Head of Growth: banned words, claims, naming, landing page, tracking. A log of what launched, where, and when.
 Builds. Landing page variants and new funnel pages in GoHighLevel or ClickFunnels. Email sequences and automations in ActiveCampaign. Split-test setup. You build from the copywriter's text to the Head of Growth's brief.
 Video editors. Day-to-day management of the editor pool: the weekly meeting, the flow of briefs, turnaround and revision targets, onboarding, screening applicants and tracking the bonus scheme. The Senior Direct Response Marketer approves the creative; you keep it moving.
 Head of Growth support. Keeping every deliverable and deadline visible and on track, and flagging anything that is going to be late before it is. Booking recording sessions, running the meeting calendar, onboarding new starters, managing tool access and subscriptions.
 Automation. We use Claude, ChatGPT and similar tools every day. Anything repeatable, whether that is reporting, QA checks, drafting procedures or reconciling data, is yours to automate.

Who We Are

North Vector Dynamics is a Canadian-owned and controlled defence technology company specializing in precision interception, autonomy, and advanced propulsion. NVD is building a full-spectrum missile capability, from counter-UAS solutions to hypersonics, designed to serve and defend NATO member states and their allies and partners.

About the Role

North Vector Dynamics is building next-generation unmanned systems, and the quality of our platforms depends on the people who build them. We’re looking for a UAS Technician to join our assembly and manufacturing team: working hands-on with airframes, avionics, propulsion systems, and payloads to bring our vehicles from components to flight-ready condition. This is a role built for someone who is technically sharp, detail-oriented, and hungry to develop their skills in a fast-moving environment. You’ll be part of a small, close-knit production team working directly alongside engineers and responsible for the quality of what leaves our floor. If you’re mechanically and electronically capable, take genuine pride in your work, and want to build the kind of systems you’ll one day see in the field, this role was written for you.

What You’ll Do

• Perform hands-on assembly of UAS platforms: including airframe construction, avionics installation, wiring harness integration, propulsion system build-up, and payload fitment, working to engineering drawings and assembly instructions.

• Execute QA inspection and functional testing at each stage of assembly: conducting pre-flight checks, bench testing of avionics and electrical systems, continuity checks, and final acceptance testing before vehicles are released for flight operations.

• Manage and maintain accurate bill of materials (BOM) records: tracking component usage, flagging discrepancies between as-built configurations and engineering documentation, and supporting engineering change order (ECO) processes.

• Support inventory management: receiving incoming components and materials, performing incoming inspection, maintaining stock accuracy, and coordinating with procurement and engineering to identify shortfalls and manage consumables.

• Document build records, test results, and non-conformances in our quality management system, maintaining full traceability from components to completed vehicles.

• Identify and escalate build issues, component defects, and design-for-manufacturability concerns to engineering; you’ll be a key feedback loop between the shop floor and the design team.

• Support rework and repair activities on returned or fielded vehicles: diagnosing faults, replacing components, and restoring platforms to serviceable condition.

• Contribute to continuous improvement of our assembly processes, work instructions, and quality procedures as our production scales.

• Step into whatever the mission demands: this is a startup, and no two weeks will look the same.

What You Bring

Required

• Practical hands-on experience with mechanical and electrical assembly: either through formal technical training, prior employment in a manufacturing or repair environment, or a demonstrated personal track record working with UAVs, RC systems, or similar electromechanical platforms.

• A methodical, quality-first approach to assembly work: you work to procedure, take care with your builds, and understand that precision matters when systems will fly.

• Ability to read and interpret engineering drawings, assembly instructions, wiring diagrams, and bills of materials.

• Basic competency with common hand tools, torque tools, soldering equipment, and electronic test equipment (multimeters, oscilloscopes, power supplies).

• Comfort with inventory and parts management: tracking components, identifying shortfalls, and maintaining accurate records.

• Attention to detail and a low error rate: you catch your own mistakes and flag others’ before they become problems.

• Eligibility for a Government of Canada security clearance; active clearance is a significant asset.

• A builder’s mindset: you take ownership of your work and look for ways to improve how things are done, not just complete the task in front of you.

Preferred

• Post-secondary education or certification in aviation maintenance technology, electronics technology, mechanical engineering technology, or a closely related technical discipline.

• Prior experience in a UAS, aerospace, or defence manufacturing or MRO environment.

• Familiarity with AS9100 or ISO 9001 quality management frameworks and the documentation discipline they require.

• Experience with ERP or MRP systems for inventory tracking, BOM management, and production order processing.

• A practical background with UAS systems, whether professional or amateur: if you’ve built, flown, maintained, and repaired your own aircraft, we want to hear from you.

Why North Vector Dynamics

• Real ownership from day one: the systems and processes you help build will be foundational to how this company operates for years to come.

• A tight-knit, high-calibre team that moves fast, holds each other to a high standard, and doesn’t waste time on bureaucracy for its own sake.

Vous devrez clarifier les besoins dans un contexte d’incertitude, livrer rapidement une première solution de recherche fonctionnelle et la faire évoluer grâce à des cycles de rétroaction courts. Si vous aimez créer des systèmes à partir de zéro, avez à cœur la performance et la pertinence des résultats, et souhaitez que votre travail soutienne les décisions quotidiennes dans une variété de secteurs, nous aimerions vous rencontrer.

Ce que vous ferez

 - Concevoir et développer la plateforme de recherche et de récupération de données de bout en bout de MaintainX — des pipelines d’indexation et systèmes de ranking jusqu’aux couches de requêtes orientées IA.

 - Collaborer avec les équipes produit et les experts métiers afin de modéliser la recherche à travers les entités clés telles que les ordres de travail, les actifs et les procédures, en garantissant des résultats hautement pertinents.

 - Livrer rapidement, itérer rapidement, lancer des versions initiales, recueillir des retours et améliorer continuellement.

 - Exploiter et optimiser des systèmes distribués en garantissant fiabilité, performance et scalabilité en conditions réelles.

 - Piloter les décisions d’architecture en équilibrant justesse, performance et maintenabilité à long terme.

 - Gérer les intégrations entre les systèmes de recherche et les sources de données amont.

 - Explorer la recherche sémantique, la récupération vectorielle et l’amélioration de la pertinence via l’IA en utilisant des outils modernes de machine learning.

 - Participer aux astreintes (actuellement pendant les heures ouvrées).

À propos de vous:

 - Expérience pratique dans la conception, le développement et l’exploitation de systèmes de recherche en production de bout en bout — incluant l’indexation, l’exécution des requêtes, l’optimisation de la pertinence et l’infrastructure — avec des technologies telles que Elasticsearch, OpenSearch, Lucene, Solr ou équivalent.

 - Bonne compréhension des embeddings, du chunking et des stratégies de récupération d’information.

 - Maîtrise des optimisations spécifiques à la recherche : analyseurs, BM25, dimensionnement des shards, santé des clusters et optimisation de la pertinence.

 - Capacité à mener un système de l’implémentation au déploiement et à l’exploitation en production, en intervenant sur les services backend, les pipelines de données et les points d’intégration si nécessaire.

 - Un niveau avancé de l'anglais, à l'oral et à l'écrit, est requis puisque la personne devra diriger des gestionnaires d'ingénierie de plateforme répartis sur plusieurs équipes, présenter les priorités techniques à des parties prenantes exécutives, et s'aligner quotidiennement avec des leaders d'ingénierie situés à l'extérieur du Québec.

Atouts supplémentaires:

 - Expérience dans l’évaluation et l’amélioration de la pertinence des résultats de recherche à l’aide d’analyses qualitatives et de métriques quantitatives.

 - Expérience dans le déploiement de systèmes backend intégrant l’IA ou des LLM.

 - À l’aise avec les outils d’IA modernes comme GPT, Copilot ou Cursor pour améliorer la productivité et optimiser le développement.

 - Compréhension des environnements multi-tenant et de la sécurité des données, incluant les ACL, les contrôles d’accès au niveau des champs et la partition sécurisée des index.

 - Expérience dans la mise en place d’outils d’observabilité et de métriques de succès pour surveiller la performance, l’utilisation et l’impact des systèmes.

Who we are
 About Stripe
 About the team
 The Stripe Marketing organization is undergoing a fundamental transformation in how it works. We're building a team of Forward Deployed AI Accelerators (FDAs) embedded directly with marketing cohorts to make AI the default mode for all work — not an occasional tool, but the foundation of how every marketer at Stripe executes.
 Today, marketers are already achieving remarkable results — building their own data dashboards, creating agents that compress multi-day processes, and authoring tools that accelerate workflows. The FDA team exists to take what's working and systematically scale it across the entire marketing organization.
 What you'll do
 As a Forward Deployed AI Accelerator, you'll be embedded with a cohort of 25–45 marketers organized by functional team, shared workflow, or location. You'll build alongside them, and you'll help them fundamentally change how they operate. Your measure of success is the number of workflows you've permanently transformed and the extent to which those in your cohort start any task with an AI tool.
 Responsibilities
 Identify and document the highest-leverage workflow transformations within your cohort's day-to-day work by deeply understanding their processes and outputs
 Build custom tools, agents, automations, and skills tailored to each marketer's specific responsibilities
 Coach and partner with each marketer through a progressive journey — from awareness, to first win, to regular AI integration, to full workflow transformation, to self-sufficiency
 Teach marketers to build and iterate on their own tools over time, creating independence
 Recognize patterns across your cohort and systematically scale what works — a tool built for one marketer will be reusable for their peers
 Document every tool, playbook, and transformation pattern you build so the entire FDA team uses each other's work
 Share wins visibly within your cohort and with leadership to build momentum, inspire, and celebrate success
 Track individual and cohort progress rigorously against a defined maturity model, moving every marketer toward self-sustaining, AI-first work
 Prepare marketers for an agentic future — not just prompt writing, but designing, building, and overseeing autonomous, multi-agent workflows
 Who you are
 We're looking for people who have already lived the transformation they'll be driving for others. You've used AI to fundamentally change how work gets done, not as a novelty, but as your default operating mode.
 You are a deep AI practitioner. You build agents, automations, and tools fluently. You don't just know what AI can do in theory. You've built things that changed how real teams operate, and the people you built for actually use what you shipped. You build in real time alongside the people you support.
 You spot transformation opportunities and execute on them. You look at a team's workflows and see where AI changes the economics: where existing work can be done in a fraction of the time, or where entirely new programs become viable that weren't worth doing before. Then you build the thing, not just the slide.
 You understand marketing work. You either have direct experience in marketing or quickly learn the workflows, deliverables, tools, and pressures of your assigned cohort. You know that understanding someone's work is a prerequisite to transforming it.
 You are a pattern recognizer. When you build something that works for one person, you immediately see how it applies to others. You think in systems, not one-off solutions.
 You are a strong communicator. You explain technical concepts clearly to non-technical audiences, adapt your style to different people, and make progress visible to leadership and stakeholders.
 You are high-caliber, persistent, and versatile. Your skills and experience are valuable across the company. You're the kind of person who succeeds in many roles at Stripe.
 You bias toward action and speed. You'd rather show someone a working proof-of-concept on their own deliverable today than present a polished deck about what's theoretically possible next quarter.
 You are comfortable with ambiguity and evolution. This is a new team building a new operating model. The playbook will be rewritten as we learn. You thrive in that environment.

 Experience in a formal AI transformation role where the job was substantially about identifying opportunities for workflow transformation and executing on them with hands-on builds
 Experience helping people become more expert AI users and capable builders
